evidence.anchor: "checkpoint","accuracy-policy."+method+"."+policy
evidence.scope: Exercise RungeKutta89 with reduce-warn through the actual policy selector. With adaptive control enabled and impossible Accuracy=1e-30, StopIfAccuracyIsViolated=true must fail before the post-propagation marker, while false must warn and complete. None bypasses that accuracy demand; loose Accuracy=1e-2 must complete without an accuracy warning. Forward/backward runs and reductions from 600 to the 300-second floor are explicit cases. Completed runs must reach their signed 1800-second epoch, execute the marker, and retain all sampled step magnitudes within the configured 300..600-second bounds. These are control-flow and step-bound tests, not proof of accurate states when a warning explicitly permits violating Accuracy.

evidence.anchor: "checkpoint","accuracy-policy."+method+"."+policy
evidence.scope: Exercise RungeKutta89 with reduce-warn through the actual policy selector. With adaptive control enabled and impossible Accuracy=1e-30, StopIfAccuracyIsViolated=true must fail before the post-propagation marker, while false must warn and complete. None bypasses that accuracy demand; loose Accuracy=1e-2 must complete without an accuracy warning. Forward/backward runs and reductions from 600 to the 300-second floor are explicit cases. Completed runs must reach their signed 1800-second epoch, execute the marker, and retain all sampled step magnitudes within the configured 300..600-second bounds. These are control-flow and step-bound tests, not proof of accurate states when a warning explicitly permits violating Accuracy.

evidence.anchor: "checkpoint","accuracy-policy."+method+"."+policy
evidence.scope: Exercise RungeKutta89 with fixed through the actual policy selector. With adaptive control enabled and impossible Accuracy=1e-30, StopIfAccuracyIsViolated=true must fail before the post-propagation marker, while false must warn and complete. None bypasses that accuracy demand; loose Accuracy=1e-2 must complete without an accuracy warning. Forward/backward runs and reductions from 600 to the 300-second floor are explicit cases. Completed runs must reach their signed 1800-second epoch, execute the marker, and retain all sampled step magnitudes within the configured 300..600-second bounds. These are control-flow and step-bound tests, not proof of accurate states when a warning explicitly permits violating Accuracy.

source_conflicts.detail: The guide says SRPArea > 0, while wx and the runtime accept zero. The guide lists nonnegative Cd/Cr; wx accepts finite real values and the runtime warns for negative Cd and Cr outside [0,2]. Setting requirements are covered without declaring complete input-domain conformance.

The generic Clone documentation describes an exact copy, but the interpreter rejects any spacecraft shared by two formations. An empty Formation clones normally; a populated copy must select disjoint members. The GUI now explains this before rebuilding. Exact populated Formation cloning remains an unresolved documentation/runtime conflict; its corrected-copy test is not counted as an exact-copy proof.

The shipped Mission Tree guide says Delete does not confirm. Qt currently presents Yes/Cancel and preserves source on Cancel. The suite asserts the current explicit confirmation workflow; this interaction difference remains unresolved rather than claiming an identical archived NASA replay.

FRR-16.9.3 and the help LSKFilename field describe editable GUI/script access. The current engine marks LSK_FILE_NAME deprecated and read-only in IsParameterReadOnly and its SetStringParameter branch ignores writes. The current Qt panel does not offer an editable LSK field. No pass or retirement is inferred; baseline reconciliation and intended supported behavior remain open.

supported_gui_route_progress.historical_intent: SPICE leap-second kernel name and location; shipped help documents SolarSystem.LSKFilename
supported_gui_route_progress.current_documented_behavior: SolarSystem setter throws a deprecation exception and explicitly requires LSK_FILE in startup settings; fresh process initializes this setting
supported_gui_route_progress.detail: New bounded GUI evidence uses the supported startup/export/restart route. The shipped help still lists LSKFilename, and its mission-script setter is not restored or qualified. This discrepancy remains explicit and is not full NASA conformance.

source_conflicts.detail: FRR-14.7.3 requires a separate minimum-error-tolerance setting. Current BulirschStoer marks MinimumTolerance read-only and deprecated; its setter warns that the field has no effect and returns the ordinary tolerance. Existing BulirschControls asserts the deprecated field is absent. No source-requirement retirement or equivalence is inferred.

The ForceModel Order allowed-values table says Degree <= Order, while the wx GUI rejects Degree < Order and HarmonicField diagnostics state Order <= Degree. GravityField runtime truncates an excessive Order during initialization. The new Qt pending-model validator follows the wx GUI and rejects Order > Degree before commit. The published/local help inequality remains a recorded source discrepancy; no full degree/order/file-limit qualification is inferred.

The shipped mathematical specification prints N_nm = sqrt((n-m)!(2n+1)!/(n+m)!), which gives N_20 = sqrt(120). Its mean-square normalization discussion and the runtime zonal normalization V[n][0] = sqrt(2n+1) instead give sqrt(5). The independent equatorial J2 fixture uses the latter normalized basis (C20=-J2/sqrt(5)); no assertion of consistency with the printed factorial expression or general scientific qualification is made. The source text is preserved and authoritative baseline/erratum reconciliation remains open.

The shipped variational-equations section defines delta x using dotted state variables, then uses delta dot x=A delta x. Its definite-integral STM equation also reverses the earlier argument order and omits the identity term, giving zero at coincident endpoints, while the immediately following initial condition explicitly requires Phi(t0,t0)=I. The new oracle follows the explicit differential equation and identity initial condition. Source text is retained; authoritative equation/notation reconciliation remains open.

The shipped tutorial introductory paragraph assigns Longitude, Latitude, Altitude to 45,270,0.1 respectively, while the following explicit steps assign Latitude45 and Longitude270. Latitude270 violates the documented/runtime latitude range. Tests follow the labeled fields, valid latitude range and explicit ordered steps. Original source is preserved; authoritative example erratum remains open.

Historical FRR!E220 and E228-E238 include user-body Keplerian/two-body orbit propagation and orbital-element settings. The shipped guide restricts custom-body PosVelSource to SPICE, and the runtime explicitly throws deprecation errors for the two-body element setters while marking them read-only. The workbook is preserved and no removed capability or retirement status is assumed; authoritative requirements reconciliation remains open.
Historical Origin setting is unsupported by the current documented SPK CentralBody behavior and intentionally inactive engine setter. No origin coverage credit.

Historical distinct rotation drift-rate setting is unreconciled with current linear W = W0 + RotationRate*d. RotationConstant is an angle, not angular acceleration; parent and drift row receive no passing credit.

Historical workbook labels RMAG read-only, while the current shipped Spacecraft calculation table marks it settable. Existing bounded algebraic read proof remains valid; no read-only setter/GUI enforcement credit is inferred.

Historical SemilatusRectum row is read-only. Current Spacecraft calculation table contains both Y and N settable entries, while the current parameter constructor marks it settable. No passing row or read-only enforcement credit is assigned pending reconciliation.

The ChemicalTank guide describes strictly-positive FuelMass, Pressure and Volume, while current setters admit zero subject to other tank constraints. This batch qualifies selected positive writes, negative/nonfinite rejection and capacity checks; it supplies no general zero-state qualification. Reconciliation remains open.

The historical requirement lists POV spacecraft models; the available current NASA spacecraft visualization guide explicitly says only3DS. The Qt chooser offers3DS andOBJ. POV requirement applicability is unresolved; no POV coverage or retirement is claimed.

Historical FRR-30.4.1 specifies right-justified columns. The current bundled guide calls LeftJustify Off centered, while native stream formatting uses right alignment. The tests check the historical requirement/native behavior; the guide wording conflict remains open.

The guide says Precision and ColumnWidth are greater than1; the native setters accept positive integers including1. Selected native GUI bounds are tested, with guide/API disagreement unresolved. No core range change is made.

FRR!E506/E513/E536 historically say EA/MA/HA read/write. The bundled current Calculation Parameters Settable column says N; all three native constructors use isSettable=false. Current readonly calculation/rejection cases do not qualify the historical writable scope. No core mutability change or retirement is inferred.

Historical E519/E520 mark position magnitude/semilatus rectum readonly. Native RMAG/SemilatusRectum are settable, and the guide marks both settable in its main table; a duplicate guide entry marks SemilatusRectum N. Current setter/readback can be exercised, but historical mutability remains unresolved. Prior versioned E519 read/calculation component evidence is retained; it does not qualify readonly enforcement.

FRR!E404 says error/stop when data cannot support requested order. The current bundled OEM guide first attempts reduced order, then errors if that fails. A10-second three-point arc requests7 and is expected to write degree2/endpoints. This current-behavior proof cannot close the historical mandatory-error requirement.

FRR!E330/E634 and the current GroundTrack guide use skipped-step wording, while the preserved frequency7 check and native OrbitPlot modulo logic implement an every-Nth integration-step period. Both scopes are explicitly uncredited. Interpretive resolution/current NASA test-plan evidence remains open.

Available historical FRC!E103 calls Nonlinear Constraint a cost-function command; current bundled NASA guide defines constraints, while Minimize defines the objective. No equivalence or cost-function credit is inferred.

Historical FRC!E54 says EndTarget ends an optimization sequence; the bundled Target guide defines Target/EndTarget as a Target sequence. Selected Target behavior is tested, but historical optimization wording is not credited or silently rewritten.

Historical FRC!E97 lists a real number under Achieve control variables. The bundled Achieve guide explicitly excludes numbers as Goal while allowing real numbers as desired value Arg1. Actual Goal picker rejection of17 and desired literal9/1006 do not resolve that historical LHS/RHS ambiguity; no literal-Goal coverage is credited.

Historical FRC!E51 lists a real number as a Vary control. The bundled Vary guide explicitly excludes numbers as UserSelectedControl while permitting numeric InitialGuess. Literal-control rejection and configured numeric guesses do not resolve that historical distinction; this row remains uncredited.

The For Options table and runtime require a Variable index; general Remarks allow resource parameters for Index while also excluding parentheses. Scalar/array range operands are qualified separately. Resource/array index acceptance is not inferred, and this unresolved guide inconsistency is not silently rewritten.

The bundled language guide specifies left-to-right logical evaluation; the runtime explicitly groups higher-precedence AND clauses before OR. New mixed-chain diagnostics record both truth models. Neither an engine precedence rewrite nor complete NASA conformance is inferred from this unresolved primary-source conflict. Public source pages were not retrievable during this review.

The bundled Save guide is under construction. Selected export/reload capabilities do not resolve exact historical filename conformance; E135 remains uncredited.

Selected right-hand goal operands are qualified; variable/array left-hand conditions and arbitrary scalar classes remain uncredited, not silently implemented.

The bundled guide describes String-only String assignments and FRC!E177 requires compatible/equivalent types. Assignment::Validate intentionally permits numeric and object-name conversion to String (bug1340), except selected time strings. Current conversion policy is not rewritten from conflicting sources; selected rejected array/string/real combinations are bounded evidence, not strict rejection of every unequal runtime type.
